item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Thu Oct 1, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Alice Bucknell, Art Talk — Thu Oct 1, 5:30 PM — UC Davis
item.description:
Alice Bucknell, an artist whose work explores the affective dimensions of video games, will give a talk as part of The California Studio: Manetti Shrem Artist Residencies in the Maria Manetti Shrem Art Studio Program at UC Davis. A Los Angeles-based artist, writer and educator, Bucknell explores video games as interfaces for understanding complex systems, relationships, and forms of knowledge. They are interested in the limits of scientific knowledge and systems thinking, the weird possibilities of play, and the ecological dimensions of games that can dissolve binaries like humans versus environment, natural versus synthetic intelligence, and self vs world.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: "The Works of Our Hands," Related in Life and Design — Fri Oct 2 — The Artery
item.description:
The Artery presents “The Works of Our Hands,” Related in Life and Design, featuring Amina Harris, Patti Harris, and Shoshana Zeldner. The exhibit extends from October 2 to 26, with the reception on Friday, October 9, 6-9 pm coinciding with the Davis Second Friday ArtAbout. The Works of Our Hands features three family members, each having distinctive art forms. Amina Harris’s unique jewelry incorporates artifacts from ancient to modern times. Amina’s recent trip to Morocco inspired this exhibit. Patti, Amina’s sister, shows her 3-dimensional collages, using industrial design, natural materials and vintage objects. Shoshana, Amina’s daughter, creates sculptures that breath with life, exploring the relationship between the body and the subtle experiences that take place within.
Source: The Dirt

Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!

item.title: Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington — Tue Sep 29, 12:00 PM — UC Davis Design Museum
item.description:
The UC Davis Design Museum opens its 2026-2027 season with Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington which opens on Sept. 29 and runs through Nov. 20. Collaboration is at the heart of textile making and this idea is explored in a display of work by UK based artist Setterington. Through textiles the artist challenges contemporary issues in society and how stitch can be used to commemorate people and communities. She has worked with underserved communities across the globe, including the UK, India, Bangladesh, Brazil and USA. She draws on popular culture and textile history to raise awareness of societal issues. Themes range from sustainability, place, well-being and identity and belonging. This exhibition is co-sponsored by the Maria Manetti Shrem Institute for Sustainable Design, Fashion & Textiles.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Yolo Co. Voter Forum — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — Richard Brunelle Performance Hall
item.description:
by: Lorna Carriveau, League of Women Voters
League of Women Voters Forums Coming Soon
The League of Women Voters of Yolo County will be hosting multiple public, nonpartisan forums in September and October in advance of the general election on November 3.
The League’s first forum in Davis, on Thursday, Sep. 30, will be a nonpartisan voter education forum focusing on Proposition 39. Proposition 39, known as the Prohibit Voting Without Government-Issued ID initiative, aims to require all voters in California to present government-issued identification when they submit their ballot and to prove U.S. citizenship at the time they register to vote. This initiative is designed to create a new voter ID requirement and a new citizenship documentation process for voter registration. Proposition 39 increases the documentation requirements for eligible citizens to participate in elections in an effort to prevent non-citizen voting.

item.title: Banned Books Week — Sun Oct 4 — CA
item.description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.

item.title: maptimeDavis: Accessible Mapmaking — Fri Oct 30, 10:00 AM — DataLab Classroom
item.description:
Learn about accessible mapmaking and points to consider to ensure your maps are accessible. Also, learn about new UC Davis Health map with 3D printing, and UC Davis Campus map & Spatial Audio Wayfinding map! Come with questions on how to ensure that your maps work well for a variety of audiences.
Speaker: Josh Hori

item.title: Zombie Bike Parade — Sat Oct 31, 4:00 AM — Community Park
item.description:
The Zombie Bike Parade Everyone is welcome at Community Park for the festival: on foot, on any wheels, in a wheelchair or powerchair, or pushing a stroller. The official bike parade is different. It rides just under five miles at a regular biking pace, so it is for bicycles (including e-bikes, cargo bikes, tandems and bike trailers) and only for riders who can keep that pace for the whole route. Helmets are required under 18 and strongly encouraged for everyone. If the parade is not the right fit, stay at Community Park: the shows, the entertainment stations and the 2:30 p.m. skydiving finale all happen there.

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Sep 30, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Sep 30, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
